findings: The November canonical capture is a migration-title and two-platform navigation index. It verifies the iOS and Android variant links and v3.0.0 purpose. It contains no migration steps or variant behavior.

The May 1, 2026 historical guide describes existing pre-3.0.0 iOS and Android SDK migrations. iOS v3 needs iOS 13+, Android v3 needs Android 8/API 26+, compared with the respective 2.x iOS 11+/Android API 21+ floors. SDK discovery changes to reader-type configs, process calls move to confirm names, and readReusableCard is removed in favor of the SDK create/collect/confirm SetupIntent sequence.

The May iOS guide says cancellation reports SCPErrorCanceled, discovery completes at connectReader invocation, a failed connection requires another discovery call to resume discovery, and a previously discovered reader can be passed to connect without ongoing discovery. Busy errors move to an internal command queue. Builder error handling differs in Swift and Objective-C, and the reconnection delegate receives the reader.

May places Android permission checks at discovery. Location applies to any discovery config and Bluetooth only to BluetoothDiscoveryConfiguration. Bluetooth or USB stays CONNECTING during a required update and reports connected and ready after successful completion. Android Serializable guidance applies to Parcel access and recommends against persistence across SDK versions.
historical_claims_to_preserve: The prior May 1 capture remains the full evidence for v3.0.0 and its platform minima, despite a 2025 filename suffix. The historical offline private-preview sequence is Stripe backend account enablement, then SDK reader disconnect/reconnect. Offline-created PaymentIntent stripeId on iOS and id on Android can be null.

The Android list removes reader/listener/capture/configuration fields and redirects fingerprints to server-side SDKs. Preserve the historical two method renames and iOS renamed error types separately. Use separate current SDK or offline guides for newer-version rules.
conflicts: The summary's 'only rename, behavior unchanged' wording applies the Android evidence to iOS. The May iOS section explicitly preserves parameters and also renames both error types. Qualify the language independently of the November index.

The mapped summary omits historical offline enablement and reconnection qualification and states CONNECTING without Bluetooth/USB scope. Capture those boundaries without using a historical private-preview notice to assert current access.
